name: Rami Martinez
headline: Software Engineer
summary: Software engineer: four years at JPMorgan Chase on a customer-facing account-opening application (Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, React, TypeScript), after five years in hospital informatics. Ships AI applications end to end, with tests, audit trails and privacy designed in.

roles.title: Software Engineer II
bullets: Helped launch a customer-facing account-opening application that cut the average time to open an account from more than an hour to about 15 minutes.

Owned three of its services until handoff: a Kafka-to-SSE adapter streaming application status and eligibility to the browser, an aggregator that bundles internal-system data into one response, and their proxy.

Served six months as interim lead for eight engineers (code review, mentoring, sprint ceremonies, roadmap planning with product) and shipped the MVP of a deceased-notification tool: a customer or beneficiary reports a death online in a few steps and an agent collects the documents and handles closures or transfers.

Built a drag-and-drop generator for the internal UI component library: engineers compose a page and download a starter project, so new developers learn the component syntax and coding standards from generated code.

roles.title: Software Engineer I
bullets: Built Java Spring Boot microservices and integrated enterprise APIs; led the design, testing and release of a React/TypeScript interface with Redux.

roles.title: Business Informatics III
bullets: Worked to cut referral cycle time from order to scheduled appointment in specialty and radiology departments by gathering clinic requirements and coordinating Epic Referrals and Cadence enhancements with analysts.
Trained 600+ staff across 100+ departments on Epic Referrals and Cadence workflows.
Carried out user acceptance testing for Epic upgrades, documenting defects and supporting their resolution.

projects.name: Caduceus
projects.stack: Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, FHIR, Cloud Run
bullets: Prior-authorization agent for a simulated health system: reads the faxed referral, checks the record against the insurer's policy text, asks the clinician only for what's missing and drafts the request for specialist approval.

Keeps patient data inside the clinic: a local model de-identifies text before it reaches the drafting model; 181 identifiers planted across the test suite, none reached the outside model. 200+ tests, hash-chained audit log.

projects.name: Lattice
projects.stack: Rust, React, TypeScript, ROS 2, Gazebo, MuJoCo, PostgreSQL
bullets: Robot-fleet control plane that keeps a mission's objective when the route or the body changes: a Rust core plans, holds detours and handoffs for approval and signs commands, and an agent on each robot verifies them.
Three recorded simulation runs (blocked aisle, rover-to-quadruped handoff, two-rover handoff) with no completed inspection repeated; evaluations published with the code.

projects.name: 0VERTRAINED
projects.stack: React, Vite, Netlify Functions, Supabase, Web Push
bullets: Training ledger for athletes who lift and race, built alone: per-metric arbitration between Oura and Whoop, a daily readiness verdict from a week of HRV against a four-week baseline, and a server-routed LLM coach.
In beta on version 19.6; 2,030 automated tests, row-level security on every table, encrypted wearable tokens.
